title: MBABench-2.0: Evaluating AI Agents on Constructing Financial Spreadsheets Beyond Simple Verifiability
title_zh: MBABench-2.0：超越简单可验证性，评估 AI 智能体构建财务电子表格的能力

paragraphs.en: Finance is a major sector of the economy. In the U.S., government agencies attribute $ 1.4 1.4 trillion of GDP to the financial sector, at 4.9 % 4.9\% of the entire economy [ 21 ] . Among the tools the sector relies on, spreadsheets are the lingua franca of modern finance: valuation, forecasts, audit, and numerous other key financial workflows all rest on spreadsheet software [ 3 , 4 ] . As advances in large language model (LLM) agents accelerate, fueling the hope for agents to automate knowledge work, spreadsheet workflows emerge as a natural and pertinent testbed for their proficiency in financial work.
paragraphs.zh: 金融是经济中的一个重要部门。 在美国，政府机构将1.4万亿美元的GDP归因于金融部门，占整个经济的4.9% [21]。 在该部门所依赖的工具中，电子表格是现代金融的通用语言：估值、预测、审计以及众多其他关键财务工作流程都依赖于电子表格软件 [3, 4]。 随着大语言模型（LLM）智能体的进展不断加速，点燃了用智能体实现知识工作自动化的希望，电子表格工作流程成为检验智能体财务工作能力的自然且贴切的试验场。

paragraphs.en: A flurry of spreadsheet benchmarks have been proposed as a result. The overwhelming majority, however, evaluate agents on fill-in-the-blank style tasks [ 16 , 11 , 6 , 12 ] . There, agents are asked to extract answers to specific questions or to recover a few tampered formulas in an otherwise correct spreadsheet; even SpreadsheetBench 2 [ 31 ] derives its tasks from complete workbooks with parts removed and largely grades whether the computed values match the reference. This evaluation protocol misses the central, mundane, and time-consuming part of financial spreadsheet workflow — the modeling decisions, format design, and sheet layout that experts toil through to build a high-quality spreadsheet from scratch . Figure 1 illustrates this difference. Far fewer benchmarks [ 19 , 13 , 28 ] evaluate this spreadsheet construction capability of LLM agents.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，涌现出了大量的电子表格基准测试。 然而，其中绝大多数都是通过填空式任务来评估智能体 [ 16 , 11 , 6 , 12 ] 。 在这些任务中，智能体被要求提取特定问题的答案，或在一个原本正确的电子表格中恢复少数被篡改的公式；即使是 SpreadsheetBench 2 [ 31 ] ，其任务也是从删除了部分内容的完整工作簿中衍生而来，并且主要依据计算值是否与参考值匹配来评分。 这种评估协议忽略了财务电子表格工作流中核心、平凡且耗时的部分——即专家从零开始构建高质量电子表格时反复推敲的建模决策、格式设计和表格布局。 图 1 展示了这一差异。 评估大语言模型智能体这种电子表格构建能力的基准测试 [ 19 , 13 , 28 ] 则要少得多。

paragraphs.en: Evaluating this financial spreadsheet construction poses two main challenges. The first concerns data availability . Finance is broad, encompassing investment banking, private equity, corporate finance, wealth management, and more, making it costly to assemble a sufficiently large and diverse set of tasks. Exacerbating the issue, real financial data is often sensitive and proprietary, which precludes public release. Reflecting these constraints, BankerToolBench [ 13 ] focuses exclusively on investment banking, whereas MBABench-1.0 [ 28 ] covers finance broadly but releases only 38 38 of its 202 202 tasks, citing intellectual-property restrictions. The second challenge concerns evaluation . In practice, spreadsheets serve not just as calculation devices but also as collaborative communication tools, and miscommunication can be costly. During Barclays’ 2008 2008 acquisition of Lehman Brothers assets, a junior associate accidentally led the bank to purchase 179 179 additional assets due to lack of clarity in the spreadsheet [ 7 ] . This communicative role of spreadsheets naturally demands additional quality criteria such as readability and auditability, beyond mere accuracy. To capture these broader quality criteria, GDPval [ 19 ] employs experts to manually annotate pairwise preferences, but this approach is costly to scale and hard to reproduce. The community thus needs a public benchmark that offers both breadth and scale in its tasks, and evaluates quality criteria beyond accuracy in a transparent, scalable manner.
paragraphs.zh: 评估这类金融电子表格的构建面临两大主要挑战。 第一个挑战涉及数据可用性。 金融领域涵盖面广，包括投资银行、私募股权、公司金融、财富管理等，这使得收集一个足够大规模且多样化的任务集合成本很高。 更糟糕的是，真实的金融数据往往是敏感且专有的，无法公开发布。 受这些限制的影响，BankerToolBench [ 13 ] 仅聚焦于投资银行领域，而 MBABench-1.0 [ 28 ] 虽然广泛覆盖金融领域，但由于知识产权限制，仅发布了其 202 202 个任务中的 38 38 个。 第二个挑战涉及评估。 在实际应用中，电子表格不仅是计算工具，还是协作沟通的工具，而沟通不畅可能造成高昂代价。 在巴克莱银行 2008 2008 年收购雷曼兄弟资产的过程中，一名初级员工由于电子表格表述不清，导致该银行误购了 179 179 项额外资产 [ 7 ] 。 电子表格的这种沟通属性自然要求除准确性之外的其他质量标准，例如可读性和可审计性。 为了捕捉这些更广泛的质量标准，GDPval [ 19 ] 采用专家人工标注成对偏好，但这种方法难以规模化且难以复现。 因此，社区需要一个公开的基准，其任务既要具备广度与规模，又能以透明、可扩展的方式评估准确性之外的质量标准。

paragraphs.en: This paper presents MBABench-2.0, a fully public benchmark comprising 101 101 spreadsheet construction tasks that cover key financial fields including investment banking, corporate financial planning and analysis (FP&A), commercial banking, and wealth management. While the spreadsheet quality beyond calculation accuracy may seem nebulous, the industry in fact largely agrees on principles that one should follow in a high-quality spreadsheet [ 9 ] (e.g., stating units, or consolidating key assumptions in one place). Where these conventions leave room for interpretation, firms typically codify their own house standards for employees to follow. We therefore propose a taxonomy of 129 129 criteria across 12 12 categories, with the conventions left open fixed in house standards that every agent receives. For instance, No hardcoded numbers in formulas requires all calculations to use one coherent set of assumptions, and Numbers right-aligned requires numerical values to be right-aligned. Similar to Lau et al. [13] and Yen et al. [28] , MBABench-2.0 employs a validated agentic judge to evaluate these quality criteria at scale. Following the difficulty taxonomy of Yen et al. [28] , about half of our tasks are Medium-Hard ( 30 30 ) or Hard ( 20 20 ), the tiers where frontier agents still struggle. In comparison, we have 7.5 7.5 × and 10 10 × as many difficult tasks as MBABench-1.0’s public tasks ( 4 4 and 2 2 , respectively). These tasks examine long-horizon model building ability, with estimated build times of up to 𝟑𝟑 \mathbf{33} hours for a modeler with 3 3 + years of experience. Figure 4 illustrates one such task: only one agent answers all its questions correctly, and even the numerically correct workbook falls short of our quality criteria. Finally, we conduct a large-scale evaluation of spreadsheet construction: we evaluate over 20 20 agents (from selected combinations of 8 8 models × \times 4 4 agentic harness types) for a total of 2 2 K long-horizon trajectories, exceeding $ 57 57 K in agent inference cost alone.
paragraphs.zh: 本文提出 MBABench-2.0，这是一个完全公开的基准，包含 101 101 个电子表格构建任务，涵盖投资银行、企业财务规划与分析（FP&A）、商业银行和财富管理等关键金融领域。 虽然电子表格在计算准确性之外的质量似乎难以界定，但业界实际上对高质量电子表格应遵循的原则已有广泛共识 [ 9 ]（例如标注单位，或将关键假设集中在一处）。 在这些惯例留有解释空间的地方，各公司通常会制定自己的内部标准供员工遵循。 因此，我们提出了一个包含 129 129 项标准、分为 12 12 个类别的分类体系，其中留待解释的惯例被固定在每位智能体都会收到的内部标准中。 例如，「公式中不得硬编码数字」要求所有计算使用一套连贯一致的假设，「数字右对齐」要求数值右对齐。与 Lau 等人 [13] 和 Yen 等人 [28] 类似，MBABench-2.0 采用经过验证的智能体评审来大规模评估这些质量标准。 遵循 Yen 等人 [28] 的难度分类体系，我们的任务中约有一半为中等偏难（ 30 30 ）或困难（ 20 20 ），即前沿智能体仍难以应对的层级。 相比之下，我们的困难任务数量分别是 MBABench-1.0 公开任务（分别为 4 4 个和 2 2 个）的 7.5 7.5 倍和 10 10 倍。 这些任务考察长时程建模能力，对于拥有 3 3 年以上经验的建模者，预计构建时间最长可达 𝟑𝟑 \mathbf{33} 小时。 图 4 展示了其中一个任务：只有一个智能体正确回答了其全部问题，即使是数值正确的工作簿也未达到我们的质量标准。 最后，我们对电子表格构建进行了大规模评估：我们评估了超过 20 20 个智能体（来自 8 8 个模型 × \times 4 4 种智能体框架类型的选定组合），总计 2 2 K 条长时程轨迹，仅智能体推理成本就超过 $ 57 57 K。

paragraphs.en: We find that even the top agent passes only 16 % 16\% of the tasks, and a substantial number of agents with weaker backbone models or harnesses pass none. Agents fall short both in numerical accuracy and in the other quality criteria. On numerical accuracy, agents perform surprisingly poorly with lower than 60 % 60\% accuracy on tasks rated Medium or harder. Most of these numerical errors stem from agents misreading the instructions (e.g., paying the full monthly salary twice per month on a bi-weekly schedule), or from a lack of professional judgment (e.g., comparing a gross profit that includes other operating income against a budget gross profit that excludes it). On the other quality criteria, agents’ failures are more varied. For example, their models are hard to modify because timelines are fixed to a specific horizon, and they often contain deeply nested formulas that are hard to audit. These results suggest that current spreadsheet agents are still far from delivering professional spreadsheets.
paragraphs.zh: 我们发现，即使是排名最高的智能体也仅通过 16 % 16\% 的任务，而相当数量的采用较弱骨干模型或运行框架的智能体则一无所过。 智能体在数值准确性以及其他质量标准方面均存在不足。 在数值准确性上，智能体的表现出奇地差，在被评为中等或更难的任务上准确率低于 60 % 60\%。 这些数值错误大多源于智能体误读指令（例如，在双周发薪制下每月支付两次整月薪水），或源于缺乏专业判断（例如，将包含其他营业收入的毛利润与不包含其他营业收入的预算毛利润进行比较）。 在其他质量标准方面，智能体的失败表现更为多样。 例如，它们的模型由于时间线被固定在特定期限而难以修改，并且常常包含难以审计的深层嵌套公式。 这些结果表明，当前的电子表格智能体距离生成专业水准的电子表格仍有很大差距。

sents.en: These results suggest that current spreadsheet agents are still far from delivering professional spreadsheets.
sents.zh: 这些结果表明，当前的电子表格智能体距离生成专业水准的电子表格仍有很大差距。

paragraphs.en: Through qualitative analysis, we find common pitfalls in agents’ attempts, revealing the ways in which agents fail in both numerical accuracy and other spreadsheet quality criteria.
paragraphs.zh: 通过定性分析，我们发现了智能体在尝试过程中的常见缺陷，揭示了智能体在数值准确性以及其他电子表格质量标准方面失败的方式。

paragraphs.en: Finance has long attracted interest from LLM benchmarks. Early benchmarks are predominantly QA-based, testing models on simple derivation or finance knowledge [ 23 , 24 , 29 , 17 , 15 ] . As LLM agents have improved, attention has shifted to spreadsheet manipulation that underpins several core finance workflows. Before the long-horizon capabilities of agents matured, SpreadsheetBench [ 16 ] , widely used during this time, examined agents on targeted manipulations of existing spreadsheets, drawn from questions on Excel forums and graded on the resulting cell values. Many subsequent evaluations follow the same pattern, focusing on summarization, QA, and a few formula edits [ 11 , 6 , 12 ] . SpreadsheetBench 2 [ 31 ] extends this to end-to-end workflows on large workbooks, but derives its tasks from complete workbooks with parts removed and, except for visualization tasks, grades whether the computed cell values match the reference. Constructing spreadsheets from scratch is part of GDPval [ 19 ] , which includes such tasks among its occupational deliverables, and is evaluated by Lau et al. [13] for investment banking and by Yen et al. [28] for finance in general. We build on this line of work with a fully public benchmark consisting of 101 101 spreadsheet construction tasks across general finance.
paragraphs.zh: 金融领域长期以来一直吸引着大语言模型基准测试的关注。 早期的基准测试主要以问答为基础，测试模型进行简单推导或掌握金融知识的能力 [ 23 , 24 , 29 , 17 , 15 ] 。 随着大语言模型智能体的不断改进，注意力已转向作为多项核心金融工作流程基础的电子表格操作。 在智能体的长时程能力成熟之前，这一时期被广泛使用的 SpreadsheetBench [ 16 ] 考察智能体对现有电子表格进行针对性操作的能力，这些电子表格取自 Excel 论坛上的问题，并根据生成的单元格值进行评分。 许多后续评估沿用相同的模式，专注于摘要、问答以及少量公式编辑 [ 11 , 6 , 12 ] 。 SpreadsheetBench 2 [ 31 ] 将其扩展到大型工作簿上的端到端工作流程，但其任务来源于删除了部分内容的完整工作簿，并且除了可视化任务外，以计算出的单元格值是否与参考值一致来评分。 从零开始构建电子表格是 GDPval [ 19 ] 的一部分，该基准将此类任务纳入其职业交付成果中，并由 Lau 等人 [13] 针对投资银行业务以及 Yen 等人 [28] 针对一般金融领域进行了评估。 我们在这一研究方向的基础上，构建了一个完全公开的基准，包含 101 101 个覆盖一般金融领域的电子表格构建任务。

paragraphs.en: Agents are increasingly expected to perform economically valuable work. The first promising domain is coding [ 5 , 10 ] , followed by computer use [ 30 , 25 ] , legal work [ 8 ] , and other occupations from manufacturing to animation [ 19 , 20 ] . As agents’ tasks become more realistic, accuracy-based evaluation no longer captures the full spectrum of desiderata in real-world work product. For example, despite advances in standard coding benchmarks, agents often produce verbose and difficult-to-maintain code [ 22 , 27 ] . GDPval [ 19 ] accounts for these high-level quality criteria in evaluation by having experts annotate pairwise preferences, at the cost of scalable evaluation. Recent coding [ 14 ] and spreadsheet benchmarks [ 13 , 28 ] tackle this with a mix of automatic graders and LLM-based judges. This work takes the latter approach: we first propose a taxonomy of quality criteria for financial spreadsheets, and then develop and validate a corresponding agentic judge system for reliable and scalable grading.
paragraphs.zh: 人们对智能体执行具有经济价值的工作的期望越来越高。 第一个有前景的领域是编程 [ 5 , 10 ] ，其次是计算机使用 [ 30 , 25 ] 、法律工作 [ 8 ] ，以及从制造业到动画等其他职业 [ 19 , 20 ] 。 随着智能体的任务变得更加贴近现实，仅基于准确率的评估已无法涵盖现实世界工作成果的全部质量诉求。 例如，尽管标准编程基准测试不断取得进展，智能体生成的代码往往冗长且难以维护 [ 22 , 27 ] 。 GDPval [ 19 ] 通过让专家标注成对偏好，在评估中纳入了这些高层次的质量标准，但代价是评估难以规模化。 近期的编程 [ 14 ] 和电子表格基准测试 [ 13 , 28 ] 通过结合自动评分器和基于 LLM 的评判者来解决这一问题。 本工作采取后一种方法：我们首先提出针对金融电子表格的质量标准分类体系，然后开发并验证了相应的智能体评判系统，以实现可靠且可扩展的评分。

paragraphs.en: The task set targets the core work of financial modelers, building a complete model from scratch, across a wide range of spreadsheet models used in finance, from company valuation and 3 3 -statement models to FP&A, debt schedules, instrument pricing, personal finance, and business analytics. With 16 16 task types across seven fields, it is broader than any comparable benchmark (Figure 3 ). About half of the tasks ( 50 50 of 101 101 ) are Medium-Hard or Hard, with estimated build times of up to 33 33 hours (Appendix B.2 ). We release the full task set, including the golden solutions.
paragraphs.zh: 该任务集瞄准金融建模师的核心工作——从零开始构建完整模型，涵盖金融领域广泛使用的各类电子表格模型，从公司估值和三表模型到 FP&A、债务时间表、金融工具定价、个人理财以及商业分析。 该任务集包含七大领域的 16 种任务类型，比任何同类基准都更为广泛（图 3）。 约一半的任务（101 个中的 50 个）属于中等偏难或困难级别，预估构建时间最长可达 33 小时（附录 B.2）。 我们发布了完整的任务集，包括标准答案。

paragraphs.en: All tasks were created by finance experts rather than derived from existing materials, which reduces the risk of data contamination. Since the tasks contain no client data or proprietary material, we can release all of them without privacy or intellectual-property restrictions. Each task consists of an input workbook (the starting file in our repository) and a golden solution with the completed financial model. The input workbook contains the task instructions, assumptions, supporting data where needed, and questions. The instructions are phrased as practitioners would phrase such a request and were refined iteratively to remove the ambiguities we identified. The questions are designed to examine whether the model is correct in all of its main results and intermediate calculations. An attempt therefore satisfies the Final calculation accuracy criterion (Section 3 ) only if it answers all questions correctly. All tasks passed a multi-stage quality assurance process with human and LLM-based review; Appendix C describes the task design and quality assurance process in detail.
paragraphs.zh: 所有任务均由金融领域专家创建，而非改编自现有材料，这降低了数据污染的风险。 由于任务中不包含任何客户数据或专有材料，我们可以不受隐私或知识产权限制地全部发布。 每个任务由一个输入工作簿（即我们代码库中的起始文件）和一个包含已完成财务模型的黄金答案组成。 输入工作簿包含任务说明、假设、所需的支持数据以及问题。 说明的措辞与从业者提出此类请求时的表述一致，并经过反复修改以消除我们发现的歧义。 这些问题旨在检验模型的所有主要结果和中间计算是否正确。 因此，只有正确回答所有问题，一次尝试才能满足最终计算准确性标准（第 3 节）。 所有任务均通过了包含人工审查和基于大语言模型审查的多阶段质量保证流程；附录 C 详细描述了任务设计与质量保证流程。

paragraphs.en: To show what the benchmark covers, we manually annotated each task with a difficulty level and a task type (Figures 2 and 3 ). Appendix B details both annotations, including a description of each task type.

paragraphs.en: An Integrated Daily Model. The three statements must agree on all 3,653 3{,}653 days. Example mistake: a $ 100 100 expense that should be but is not deducted from cash flow, which results in an error that propagates to all later days.
paragraphs.zh: 一个集成的每日模型。 三张报表必须在全部 3{,}653 天 3{,}653 天上保持一致。 错误示例：一笔 100 美元 100 的费用本应从现金流中扣除却没有扣除，导致错误传播到之后的所有天数。

sents.en: An Integrated Daily Model.
sents.zh: 一个集成的每日模型。

sents.en: The three statements must agree on all 3,653 3{,}653 days.
sents.zh: 三张报表必须在全部 3{,}653 天 3{,}653 天上保持一致。

sents.en: Example mistake: a $ 100 100 expense that should be but is not deducted from cash flow, which results in an error that propagates to all later days.
sents.zh: 错误示例：一笔 100 美元 100 的费用本应从现金流中扣除却没有扣除，导致错误传播到之后的所有天数。

paragraphs.en: Consistent Aggregates. Every monthly and yearly figure must be derived from the daily values in that period, so that numbers from days, months, and years always agree. Shortcuts that bypass the daily values break this, because months have different numbers of days. Example mistake: a cost of $ 100 100 a day should total $ 3,100 3{,}100 in January and $ 2,800 2{,}800 in February; dividing the yearly $ 36,500 36{,}500 cost across months evenly gives an incorrect cost of $ 3,041.67 3{,}041.67 per month.
paragraphs.zh: 一致的汇总。 每个月度和年度数字必须由该期间的日值推导得出，从而使日、月、年的数字始终保持一致。 绕过日值的捷径会破坏这一点，因为每个月的天数不同。 错误示例：每天 100 美元的成本在 1 月应合计为 3,100 美元，在 2 月应合计为 2,800 美元；若将全年 36,500 美元的成本平均分摊到各月，则会得出每月 3,041.67 美元的错误成本。

sents.en: Consistent Aggregates.
sents.zh: 一致的汇总。

sents.en: Every monthly and yearly figure must be derived from the daily values in that period, so that numbers from days, months, and years always agree.
sents.zh: 每个月度和年度数字必须由该期间的日值推导得出，从而使日、月、年的数字始终保持一致。

sents.en: Shortcuts that bypass the daily values break this, because months have different numbers of days.
sents.zh: 绕过日值的捷径会破坏这一点，因为每个月的天数不同。

sents.zh: 错误示例：每天 100 美元的成本在 1 月应合计为 3,100 美元，在 2 月应合计为 2,800 美元；若将全年 36,500 美元的成本平均分摊到各月，则会得出每月 3,041.67 美元的错误成本。

paragraphs.en: Calendar Conventions. Some costs are defined as a daily average but are only incurred Monday to Friday. To keep the weekly total the same, each weekday must carry 7 / 5 7/5 of the daily average and nothing on weekends. Other rules are tied to exact dates, such as annual increases on 1 1 January and a profit distribution every 12 12 April. Example mistake: for a cost averaging $ 100 100 a day, charging $ 100 100 instead of $ 140 140 on each weekday, resulting in $ 500 500 instead of $ 700 700 cost per week.
paragraphs.zh: 日历约定。 有些成本定义为日均值，但只在周一至周五发生。 为了保持每周总额不变，每个工作日必须承担日均值的 7 / 5 7/5，而周末不承担任何成本。 其他规则与确切日期挂钩，例如每年 1 1 月 1 1 日增长一次，以及每年 12 12 月 4 4 日进行一次利润分配。 错误示例：对于日均 $ 100 100 的成本，每个工作日收取 $ 100 100 而非 $ 140 140，导致每周成本为 $ 500 500 而非 $ 700 700。

sents.en: Calendar Conventions.
sents.zh: 日历约定。

sents.en: Some costs are defined as a daily average but are only incurred Monday to Friday.
sents.zh: 有些成本定义为日均值，但只在周一至周五发生。

sents.en: Example mistake: for a cost averaging $ 100 100 a day, charging $ 100 100 instead of $ 140 140 on each weekday, resulting in $ 500 500 instead of $ 700 700 cost per week.
sents.zh: 错误示例：对于日均 $ 100 100 的成本，每个工作日收取 $ 100 100 而非 $ 140 140，导致每周成本为 $ 500 500 而非 $ 700 700。

paragraphs.en: Valuation Steps. Valuing the company takes four steps: converting each future month’s cash into today’s money (discounting at the weighted average cost of capital, or WACC), estimating the company’s value for all years after the forecast (terminal value), shifting the result to the exact valuation date (roll-forward), and deducting debt and debt-like obligations while adding cash and investments (enterprise-to-equity bridge). Each step is simple, but skipping one still produces a reasonable-looking number. Example mistake: Excel’s NPV function implicitly values the cash flows as of 31 31 December 2026 2026 , but the task asks for the value on 20 20 July 2027 2027 , so the result fails to account for the growth in value over the 201 201 days between the two dates.
paragraphs.zh: 估值步骤。 对公司估值需要四个步骤：把未来每个月的现金折算成今天的钱（按加权平均资本成本，即 WACC 进行折现）、估算预测期之后所有年份的公司价值（终值）、把结果滚动调整至确切的估值日期（滚动前推）、并扣除债务及类债务义务同时加上现金和投资（从企业价值到股权价值的桥接）。 每个步骤都很简单，但即使漏掉一步，仍会得出一个看起来合理的数字。 示例错误：Excel 的 NPV 函数默认将现金流估值至 2026 年 12 月 31 日，但任务要求的是 2027 年 7 月 20 日的价值，因此该结果未能反映这两个日期之间 201 天内的价值增长。

paragraphs.en: Circular Dependencies. A common approach to estimating company value is to discount its future cash flows at the opportunity cost of the capital provided by its shareholders and lenders (WACC). However, the value of the company depends on the WACC, while the WACC is itself estimated from the value of the company’s equity. This circularity demands careful handling of circular references in the spreadsheet (e.g., starting from an initial guess and recomputing until the WACC and the company value agree). Example mistake: guessing an equity value of $ 60 60 M to compute the WACC, obtaining a valuation of $ 80 80 M, and reporting the valuation without recomputing the WACC from $ 80 80 M, so the WACC and the company value disagree.
paragraphs.zh: 循环依赖。 估算公司价值的一种常见方法是以股东和债权人提供的资本的机会成本（WACC）对公司未来现金流进行折现。 然而，公司价值取决于 WACC，而 WACC 本身又是根据公司股权价值估算的。 这种循环性要求在电子表格中谨慎处理循环引用（例如，从一个初始猜测开始，反复重新计算，直到 WACC 与公司价值一致）。 示例错误：猜测股权价值为 $ 60 60 M 并据此计算 WACC，得出估值 $ 80 80 M，然后未从 $ 80 80 M 重新计算 WACC 就直接报告该估值，导致 WACC 与公司价值不一致。

paragraphs.en: None of these requirements is hard on its own; the difficulty comes from satisfying all of them across thousands of interdependent days, starting from a workbook that contains only the inputs. Most prior benchmarks ask agents to look up an answer or repair a few formulas in a finished workbook. For example, SpreadsheetBench 2 [ 31 ] creates each task from a complete workbook by removing parts or injecting errors so that the structure of the workbook is largely provided. In contrast, to solve tasks such as DayMonthYear in MBABench-2.0, designing that structure and making sure the model is correct from the first daily balance to the final equity value is a central part of the task.
paragraphs.zh: 这些要求单独来看都不难；难点在于从一本只包含输入数据的工作簿出发，在数千个相互依赖的交易日中同时满足所有要求。 以往的多数基准测试只要求智能体查找答案或修复成品工作簿中的少量公式。 例如，SpreadsheetBench 2 [31] 通过删减部分内容或注入错误，从完整工作簿中构造每个任务，因此工作簿的结构大体上是给定的。 相比之下，要解决 MBABench-2.0 中诸如 DayMonthYear 的任务，设计这种结构并确保模型从第一天的每日余额到最终的股权价值都正确无误，本身就是任务的核心部分。

paragraphs.en: Financial modeling tasks vary widely: a 3 3 -statement model, a DCF valuation, and a working capital model serve drastically different purposes. Yet beneath this variety, good financial models share a common and codifiable standard: they should separate inputs from calculations, use transparent formulas, follow consistent formatting conventions, and include error checks so that the model is clear and maintainable to others. This commonality allows us to design a list of universal criteria that we apply to all tasks (e.g., No hardcoded numbers in formulas ). In addition, we supplement the list with conditional criteria whose applicability depends on the specific task (e.g., Single date driver ). This fixed criterion set keeps the grading scale consistent across tasks and types of financial model and allows the judge to be tested criterion by criterion (see Section 4.1 ). Our rubric thus consists of 129 129 criteria in total ( 93 93 universal and 36 36 conditional; see Figure 7 ).
paragraphs.zh: 财务建模任务千差万别：三表模型、DCF 估值和营运资金模型服务的目标截然不同。 然而在这种多样性之下，优秀的财务模型都遵循一个共同且可明确表述的标准：它们应当将输入与计算分离，使用透明的公式，遵循一致的格式规范，并包含错误检查，从而使模型对他人而言清晰且易于维护。 这种共性使我们能够设计出一组适用于所有任务的通用标准（例如，公式中不得硬编码数字）。 此外，我们还用条件性标准对清单加以补充，这些标准的适用性取决于具体任务（例如，单一日期驱动因素）。 这一固定的标准集使评分尺度在不同任务和不同类型的财务模型之间保持一致，并允许逐条标准对评判者进行测试（见第 4.1 节）。 因此，我们的评分标准共包含 129 129 条标准（其中 93 93 条通用标准和 36 36 条条件性标准；见图 7）。

paragraphs.en: Public financial modeling codes agree on principles but leave certain conventions open, such as the sign convention (e.g., whether costs are shown as negative numbers) or number formats (e.g., whether negatives appear in parentheses) [ 9 ] . Firms fix these in internal guidelines, and spreadsheet agents increasingly receive such guidelines as context [ 18 , 1 ] . We mirror this setting by specifying the standards agents are supposed to follow: every agent receives house standards, a compact markdown file written in the style of a firm’s internal guidelines (Appendix G ). Stating the target convention ensures that agents are not penalized for conventions they could not infer, and lets the judge check conformance to a known specification rather than decide whether an alternative is acceptable, which keeps verdicts comparable across agents. The rubric itself is not disclosed.
paragraphs.zh: 公共财务建模代码在原则上达成一致，但在某些约定上留有余地，例如符号约定（如成本是否显示为负数）或数字格式（如负数是否用括号表示）[ 9 ]。 企业会在内部指南中固定这些约定，而电子表格智能体也越来越多地接收此类指南作为上下文 [ 18 , 1 ]。 我们通过指定智能体应当遵循的标准来模拟这一情境：每个智能体都会收到内部标准，一份以企业内部指南风格撰写的简洁 markdown 文件（附录 G ）。 明确目标约可以确保智能体不会因其无法推断的约定而受到惩罚，并使评审者能够依据已知规范检查一致性，而不是判断某种替代方案是否可接受，从而使各智能体的判定结果具有可比性。 评分细则本身不予公开。

paragraphs.en: After annotating applicability, each task in MBABench-2.0 is graded on between 105 105 and 126 126 criteria. Each criterion is further assigned to one of 12 12 categories and one of four importance levels, from which its weight is derived. We defer details to Appendix A . This design is comprehensive , as every task is checked against the common core and against the conditional criteria its model requires, and efficient , as a new task needs only a yes/no relevance decision per conditional criterion and a new model type only the few criteria specific to it. It is also verifiable : because each criterion is defined once for all tasks, the judge can be tested on each criterion individually (Section 4.1 ). Finally, although the applicable criteria differ between tasks, each category carries the same weight in every task, which keeps the grading scale consistent across tasks and types of financial models.
paragraphs.zh: 在标注适用性之后，MBABench-2.0 中的每项任务都依据 105 至 126 条标准进行评分。 每条标准还被进一步归入 12 个类别之一和四个重要性级别之一，其权重即由此得出。 细节见附录 A。 这一设计既全面又高效：全面，是因为每项任务都对照共同核心标准以及其模型所需的条件性标准进行核查；高效，是因为一个新任务只需对每条条件性标准做出是/否的相关性判断，而一个新的模型类型只需评估专属于它的少数几条标准。 它还是可验证的：由于每条标准对所有任务只定义一次，评审者可以针对每条标准单独进行测试（第 4.1 节）。 最后，尽管各任务适用的标准不同，但每个类别在每项任务中的权重相同，这使得评分尺度在各类任务和各类财务模型之间保持一致。

sents.en: This design is comprehensive , as every task is checked against the common core and against the conditional criteria its model requires, and efficient , as a new task needs only a yes/no relevance decision per conditional criterion and a new model type only the few criteria specific to it.
sents.zh: 这一设计既全面又高效：全面，是因为每项任务都对照共同核心标准以及其模型所需的条件性标准进行核查；高效，是因为一个新任务只需对每条条件性标准做出是/否的相关性判断，而一个新的模型类型只需评估专属于它的少数几条标准。

sents.en: It is also verifiable : because each criterion is defined once for all tasks, the judge can be tested on each criterion individually (Section 4.1 ).
sents.zh: 它还是可验证的：由于每条标准对所有任务只定义一次，评审者可以针对每条标准单独进行测试（第 4.1 节）。

sents.en: Finally, although the applicable criteria differ between tasks, each category carries the same weight in every task, which keeps the grading scale consistent across tasks and types of financial models.
sents.zh: 最后，尽管各任务适用的标准不同，但每个类别在每项任务中的权重相同，这使得评分尺度在各类任务和各类财务模型之间保持一致。

paragraphs.en: As an example, consider the conditional criterion Single date driver (Figure 5 ). This criterion applies to any task with a time component and requires a single, clearly labeled anchor date that drives all time periods and dependent calculations. A spreadsheet that satisfies this criterion allows an analyst to easily shift the entire model timeline by changing a single cell, which is particularly useful when a planned transaction is postponed. Without it, the analyst would have to painstakingly update all cells that depend on the anchor date, which risks introducing mistakes.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，考虑条件性准则「单一日期驱动」（图 5）。 该准则适用于任何包含时间要素的任务，要求有一个单一的、标注清晰的主日期，由它驱动所有时间段及相关的计算。 满足该准则的电子表格使分析师只需更改一个单元格即可轻松移动整个模型的时间线，这在计划中的交易被推迟时尤为有用。 若没有该准则，分析师将不得不费力地更新所有依赖于主日期的单元格，这有引入错误的风险。

paragraphs.en: Each criterion is marked satisfied or violated. Final calculation accuracy is graded deterministically by comparing the agent’s answers to the task’s questions with the correct answers (Appendix A.4 ), as are 19 19 other criteria that fixed rules can check reliably. paragraphs.en: We evaluate each model through up to four harnesses. GUI : the LLM vendor’s own web pages (e.g., Claude Cowork). Code : Claude Code for Anthropic models and the open-sourced Codex CLI for all others. Excel : the proprietary Excel add-ins by OpenAI and Anthropic. In-house : a custom agentic harness that lets LLMs operate on spreadsheets via openpyxl . We defer details of these harnesses to Appendix I . Note that since we do not have direct access to the designs of proprietary harnesses, we do not aim to disentangle the effect of model and harness quantitatively. The results serve to ( 1 1 ) provide practically useful observations on performance of existing agents and ( 2 2 ) assess the effect of harnesses for a fixed underlying model.
paragraphs.zh: 我们通过至多四种测试框架来评估每个模型。 GUI：LLM 厂商自己的网页（例如 Claude Cowork）。 Code：Anthropic 模型使用 Claude Code，其余模型使用开源的 Codex CLI。 Excel：OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的专有 Excel 插件。 自研：一个自定义的智能体框架，让 LLM 通过 openpyxl 操作电子表格。 这些框架的细节见附录 I。 请注意，由于我们无法直接接触专有框架的设计，我们不打算定量地拆分模型与框架各自的影响。 这些结果旨在：(1 1) 为现有智能体的性能提供实际有用的观察，(2 2) 在固定底层模型的情况下评估框架的影响。

paragraphs.en: In this section, we validate the reliability of the agentic judge we employ for scalable evaluation. We approach the validation by stress-testing the judge on grading two types of attempts: (a) hand-crafted examples that satisfy or violate a specific criterion, so we can have a controlled and targeted examination of the judge’s performance on individual criteria, and (b) actual attempts by evaluated agents, so we can examine the judge’s performance on the attempt distribution that it sees at deploy time.
paragraphs.zh: 在本节中，我们对我们用于可扩展评估的智能体裁判的可靠性进行验证。 我们通过对裁判在评判两类尝试上的压力测试来进行验证：(a) 人工构造的满足或违反特定准则的示例，以便对裁判在单个准则上的表现进行受控且有针对性的检验；(b) 被评估智能体的真实尝试，以便检验裁判在部署时所面对的尝试分布上的表现。

paragraphs.en: We validated the agentic judge on each of the 109 109 criteria graded by the judge. For each criterion, we built a pair of examples by adapting a task’s golden solution: a clean example that clearly satisfies the criterion, and an erroneous example into which the task’s author manually introduced an unambiguous but not trivially detectable violation (Appendix F.2 ). We ran the judge on each of the 218 218 examples for three repetitions. Of these, 207 207 ( 95.0 % 95.0\% ) are graded correctly in all three runs and 217 217 ( 99.5 % 99.5\% ) in at least two.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在评判器所评分的 109 109 项标准中的每一项上对智能体式评判器进行了验证。 对于每项标准，我们通过改造任务的黄金解答构建了一对示例：一个明确满足该标准的干净示例，以及一个由任务作者手动引入了明确但不易被轻易察觉的违规的出错示例（附录 F.2 ）。 我们对 218 218 个示例中的每一个运行了三次评判器。 其中，207 207 个（ 95.0 % 95.0\% ）在全部三次运行中均被正确评分，217 217 个（ 99.5 % 99.5\% ）在至少两次运行中被正确评分。

paragraphs.en: To evaluate the agentic judge’s accuracy on real attempts of full tasks, we selected 12 12 attempts for annotation by human experts. Since expert annotation is extremely time-consuming, we selected the attempts from four agents spanning a range of capability (Astra-Work, Fable-Cowork, Fable-in-house, Gemini-3.8-Code). The experts graded each attempt on all applicable rubric criteria by inspecting the agent’s workbook alongside the golden solution; their annotations were afterward compared with the judge’s verdicts (Figure 10 ). Across them, the agentic judge made 1,152 1{,}152 determinations on specific rubric criteria. Of these, the judge achieved 96.4 % 96.4\% accuracy, an FPR of 1.82 % 1.82\% , an FNR of 11.1 % 11.1\% and an F 1 F_{1} of 90.4 % 90.4\% . Note that the low FPR helps the pass rate identify acceptable workbooks at a high rate.

paragraphs.en: We chose GPT-5.6 Sol as the judge’s backbone to balance the accuracy of the judge and the cost per grading. Here, we examine how closely the Sol-based judge agrees with a stronger but more expensive model, Fable 5.1. We regraded all 303 303 attempts by the same set of three agents above under the Fable-based judge. On both score and pass rate, all 3 3 agents maintain their relative rankings. The scores from both judges have a Pearson correlation of 0.901 0.901 across attempts.

paragraphs.en: Beyond judge agreement, we share additional findings on the effect of the agentic judge. ( 1 1 ) The superior judge is stricter. Fable flags a violation in 60.0 % 60.0\% of the assessments when the two judges disagree, scoring attempts 1.91 ± 0.39 1.91\pm 0.39 points lower on average. This finding aligns with the qualitative observations by the experts during the initial judge selection stage of the project, where stronger judge models flagged more violations in our runs. ( 2 2 ) No evidence of self-preference. In-house (Fable 5.1) trails Codex (GPT-6 Astra) by 11.28 11.28 points under the Sol judge and by 11.58 11.58 under the Fable judge, which differs only by a statistically insignificant 0.30 ± 0.65 0.30\pm 0.65 across 303 303 attempts.

paragraphs.en: In this section, we first discuss the main quantitative results of MBABench-2.0 and then qualitatively assess how agents fail, both in numerical accuracy and in the other 128 128 quality criteria.

paragraphs.en: We show the resulting leaderboard in Figure 6 , and find that most attempts do not meet our pass bar. Each agent has one recorded attempt per task, following common practice in end-to-end agentic evaluation (Appendix I ); we therefore report error bars to reflect the resulting uncertainty. Note that even with the same underlying model, the pass rate changes drastically (e.g., GPT-6 Astra in Codex vs. ChatGPT, or Fable 5.1 in Claude Code vs. Claude for Excel). This suggests that the harness, or the product built around it, has a major effect on the quality of the resulting spreadsheet.

paragraphs.en: Here we examine agents’ performance purely on whether they arrive at the correct numerical solution. Since Easy tasks are largely solved by the top agents, we primarily focus on tasks that are Medium and harder (see Figure 8 ). Noting the conceptual simplicity of the computation as shown in Section 2.2 , we surprisingly find that the top agent reaches only 59 % 59\% accuracy on Medium and harder tasks, and only 45 % 45\% on Hard tasks. Another noteworthy finding is that numerical accuracy is largely stable across the commercial harnesses in contrast to pass rate, showing that harnesses impact the correctness of computation less.
paragraphs.zh: 在此我们纯粹依据智能体是否得出正确的数值答案来考察其表现。 由于简单（Easy）任务已被顶尖智能体基本解决，我们主要关注中等（Medium）及更难的任务（见图 8）。 尽管 2.2 节所示的计算在概念上很简单，但我们惊讶地发现，顶尖智能体在中等及更难任务上仅达到 59% 的准确率，在困难（Hard）任务上仅为 45%。 另一个值得注意的发现是，与通过率相比，数值准确率在各商业评测框架之间基本保持稳定，这表明评测框架对计算正确性的影响较小。

paragraphs.en: In general, wall-clock solve time increases with task difficulty for all agents. Among the six agents shown, those whose solve time increases least with difficulty also perform worst (see Gemini agents in the bottom middle panel of Figure 8 , and how Pearson correlation in the bottom right correlates with agent performance), which suggests that proficient agents could recognize how difficult a task is and spend more effort correspondingly. Agents also take far less wall-clock time than the estimated human build times, although these savings must be weighed against the share of incorrect answers.
paragraphs.zh: 总体而言，对于所有智能体，实际求解时间（wall-clock solve time）随任务难度的增加而上升。 在图中所示的六个智能体中，求解时间随难度增长最少的智能体表现也最差（见图 8 底部中间面板中的 Gemini 智能体，以及底部右侧的皮尔逊相关系数与智能体表现之间的关联），这表明能力强的智能体能够识别任务的难度，并相应地投入更多精力。 智能体所需的时间也远少于估计的人工搭建时间，尽管这些节省必须与错误答案所占的比例一起权衡考虑。

paragraphs.en: In this section, we provide a complementary qualitative assessment of how agents fall short of professional standards. We discuss here the main shortcomings shared across agents (with more details in Appendix J ) and defer agent-specific failure modes to Appendix K .

paragraphs.en: On more difficult tasks, the workbooks remain complete and structurally sound, but the underlying financial models are more often incorrect. To understand why agents often build faulty financial models, we analyze every attempt that violates Final calculation accuracy and identify five main causes:
paragraphs.zh: 在更困难的任务上，工作簿仍然完整且结构良好，但底层的财务模型更常出现错误。 为了理解智能体为何经常构建有缺陷的财务模型，我们分析了每一次违反最终计算准确性的尝试，并识别出五个主要原因：

sents.en: On more difficult tasks, the workbooks remain complete and structurally sound, but the underlying financial models are more often incorrect.
sents.zh: 在更困难的任务上，工作簿仍然完整且结构良好，但底层的财务模型更常出现错误。

sents.en: To understand why agents often build faulty financial models, we analyze every attempt that violates Final calculation accuracy and identify five main causes:
sents.zh: 为了理解智能体为何经常构建有缺陷的财务模型，我们分析了每一次违反最终计算准确性的尝试，并识别出五个主要原因：

paragraphs.en: Misreading of instructions ( 44 % 44\% ) includes cases when agents paid the full monthly salary twice per month on a bi-weekly payment schedule or used simple interest when the Canadian compound method was requested.
paragraphs.zh: 指令误读（44%）包括以下情况：智能体在双周支付计划下每月支付两次全额月薪，或在要求使用加拿大复利法时使用了单利。

paragraphs.en: Lack of professional judgment ( 28 % 28\% ) arises when agents fail to follow standard practice that a human expert would apply by default. For example, agents repaid debt only from cash while a committed credit line remained unused, or compared a gross profit that includes other operating income with a budget figure that excludes it.
paragraphs.zh: 缺乏专业判断（28%）是指智能体未能遵循人类专家默认会采用的标准做法。 例如，在已承诺的授信额度尚未使用的情况下，智能体仅用现金偿还债务，或者将包含其他营业收入的毛利润与不包含该项的预算数字进行比较。

sents.en: Lack of professional judgment ( 28 % 28\% ) arises when agents fail to follow standard practice that a human expert would apply by default.
sents.zh: 缺乏专业判断（28%）是指智能体未能遵循人类专家默认会采用的标准做法。

sents.en: For example, agents repaid debt only from cash while a committed credit line remained unused, or compared a gross profit that includes other operating income with a budget figure that excludes it.
sents.zh: 例如，在已承诺的授信额度尚未使用的情况下，智能体仅用现金偿还债务，或者将包含其他营业收入的毛利润与不包含该项的预算数字进行比较。

paragraphs.en: Delivery and technical failures ( 15 % 15\% ) cover workbooks that are set up but leave every answer cell blank and generated files whose formulas show #NAME? errors once they are recalculated.
paragraphs.zh: 交付与技术故障（ 15 % 15\% ）包括那些已设置但所有答案单元格均留空的工作簿，以及重新计算后公式显示 #NAME? 错误的生成文件。

paragraphs.en: Implementation errors ( 11 % 11\% ) occur when clear instructions are provided but the financial model is nonetheless built incorrectly, as when an agent booked a payroll-tax payment as an inflow instead of an outflow or modeled 45 45 quarterly loan payments instead of 46 46 , dropping the final coupon.
paragraphs.zh: 实现错误（11%）是指指令清晰明确，但财务模型仍被构建错误的情况，例如某智能体将一笔工资税付款记录为流入而非流出，或将季度贷款还款建模为 45 期而非 46 期，从而遗漏了最后一期的票息。

paragraphs.en: Missing sense checks ( 2 % 2\% ) let implausible results pass. In one task, an agent let the share of customers using a product keep growing past 100 % 100\% , so the estimated market size came out about 50 50 × too large.
paragraphs.zh: 缺少常识性检查（2%），导致不合理的结果被放行。 在一项任务中，智能体让使用某产品的客户比例持续增长超过 100%，导致估算出的市场规模大了约 50 倍。

sents.en: Missing sense checks ( 2 % 2\% ) let implausible results pass.
sents.zh: 缺少常识性检查（2%），导致不合理的结果被放行。

sents.en: In one task, an agent let the share of customers using a product keep growing past 100 % 100\% , so the estimated market size came out about 50 50 × too large.
sents.zh: 在一项任务中，智能体让使用某产品的客户比例持续增长超过 100%，导致估算出的市场规模大了约 50 倍。

paragraphs.en: Frontier agents (the 12 12 Claude and GPT agents) violate Final calculation accuracy on fewer tasks than the eight non-frontier agents (Gemini, Grok, Kimi, and Qwen), and for different reasons: 85 % 85\% of the frontier agents’ erroneous attempts are due to misreading or a lack of professional judgment and only 13 % 13\% to errors in building or delivering the model (implementation errors or delivery and technical failures), compared with 52 % 52\% and 47 % 47\% for the non-frontier agents. Stronger agents thus make far fewer errors in building or delivering the model, but not fewer misreadings or errors of professional judgment. These two causes account for almost all erroneous attempts of the strongest agents.
paragraphs.zh: 前沿智能体（12 12 Claude 和 GPT 智能体）在“最终计算准确性”上违规的任务数量少于八个非前沿智能体（Gemini、Grok、Kimi 和 Qwen），且原因不同：前沿智能体的错误尝试中有 85 % 85\% 是由于误读或缺乏专业判断，仅有 13 % 13\% 是由于构建或交付模型时的错误（实现错误或交付与技术故障），而非前沿智能体的这两项比例分别为 52 % 52\% 和 47 % 47\%。 因此，更强的智能体在构建或交付模型时犯的错误少得多，但在误读或专业判断错误方面并未减少。 这两个原因几乎解释了最强智能体的所有错误尝试。

paragraphs.en: For example, on DayMonthYear from Section 2.2 , only Fable 5.1-Cowork answers all 130 130 questions correctly. Seven agents misread the question: they report the balance of share capital and additional paid-in capital ( 933.6 933.6 million) when the question asks for its cash-flow movement ( 26.4 26.4 million). Other errors trace back to the difficulties described there: Sol-Excel builds the daily balance sheet incorrectly, so its cash is off by about 47 47 million, and also implements the iterative WACC incorrectly; Kimi K3 in the in-house harness sidesteps the scale of the task, replacing the required daily model with a monthly approximation over 120 120 months.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，在第2.2节的“日月年”这一天，只有 Fable 5.1-Cowork 正确回答了全部 130 道问题。 七个智能体误读了问题：它们报告的是股本和额外实收资本的余额（933.6 百万），而问题问的是其现金流变动（26.4 百万）。 其他错误可追溯到前文所述的困难：Sol-Excel 错误地构建了每日资产负债表，导致其现金偏差约 47 百万，同时它还错误地实现了迭代 WACC；在内部测试框架中运行的 Kimi K3 则回避了任务的规模，用 120 个月上的月度近似替代了所需的每日模型。

paragraphs.en: Unlike failures in Final calculation accuracy , issues in quality criteria exhibit less commonality across agents, so we defer a more detailed account of agent-specific failures to Appendix K . Agents often apply presentation conventions such as freeze panes and color coding inconsistently. Beyond presentation, several failure modes on the quality criteria are shared across agents.
paragraphs.zh: 与“最终计算准确性”方面的失败不同，质量标准方面的问题在各智能体之间的共性较少，因此我们将对各智能体特有失败的更详细说明推迟到附录 K。 智能体在应用诸如冻结窗格和颜色编码等呈现规范时往往不一致。 除呈现问题之外，质量标准上的若干失败模式在各智能体之间是共通的。

paragraphs.en: The resulting models are often hard to reuse. Timelines are often fixed to the horizon specified in the task instructions, so rerunning a financial model with a later start date or a longer duration requires manual editing. On DayMonthYear , 11 11 of the 14 14 agents outside the in-house harness violate Time-period flexibility in this way. This includes Fable 5.1-Cowork, the only agent that answers all 130 130 questions correctly, but its model hardcodes the dates and the ten-year horizon and breaks when key inputs change substantially, so it violates two ultra important criteria ( Time-period flexibility and No errors under extreme-but-plausible inputs ) and therefore does not pass the task.
paragraphs.zh: 由此得到的模型往往难以复用。 时间范围通常被固定为任务说明中指定的期限，因此若要用更晚的起始日期或更长的期限重新运行财务模型，就需要手动编辑。 在 DayMonthYear，内部自有环境之外的 14 个智能体中有 11 个以这种方式违反了 Time-period flexibility。 其中包括 Fable 5.1-Cowork——它是唯一答对全部 130 个问题的智能体，但其模型硬编码了日期和十年期限，当关键输入发生重大变化时就会失效，因此它违反了两条超重要准则（Time-period flexibility 和 No errors under extreme-but-plausible inputs），因而未能通过该任务。

paragraphs.en: On harder tasks, the logic evolves into long, nested formulas that are very hard to review, which makes it particularly difficult to pinpoint where a model goes wrong. Compared with the same models in the GUI harness, the Excel add-ins produce workbooks with worse auditability: the workbooks often leave out what helps a reviewer follow the model, such as named ranges for key inputs, sources for assumptions, and notes explaining the formulas.
paragraphs.zh: 在更难的任务上，逻辑会演变成冗长且嵌套的公式，非常难以审查，这使得定位模型在何处出错尤为困难。 与在 GUI 框架中使用相同模型相比，Excel 加载项生成的工作簿可审计性更差：这些工作簿常常遗漏有助于审查者理解模型的内容，例如关键输入的命名范围、假设的来源以及解释公式的注释。

sents.en: On harder tasks, the logic evolves into long, nested formulas that are very hard to review, which makes it particularly difficult to pinpoint where a model goes wrong.

sents.en: Compared with the same models in the GUI harness, the Excel add-ins produce workbooks with worse auditability: the workbooks often leave out what helps a reviewer follow the model, such as named ranges for key inputs, sources for assumptions, and notes explaining the formulas.
sents.zh: 与在 GUI 框架中使用相同模型相比，Excel 加载项生成的工作簿可审计性更差：这些工作簿常常遗漏有助于审查者理解模型的内容，例如关键输入的命名范围、假设的来源以及解释公式的注释。

paragraphs.en: Agents often build sense checks from their own calculations, so the checks mainly confirm internal consistency. For instance, on the task TheLiquidityEngine , Astra in Codex sets each forecast to the average of the past five years and then checks that min ⁡ ( past ) ≤ forecast ≤ max ⁡ ( past ) \min(\text{past})\leq\text{forecast}\leq\max(\text{past}) . The check uses only the given data, not an outside benchmark or judgment, and, therefore, the average always passes it. The master error flag can likewise show “OK” while some of its checks are broken, which recurs in dozens of workbooks across several agents. In Grok 4.6’s attempt on the task Momentum , for instance, the flag IF(COUNTIF(D7:D30,"FAIL")=0,"OK","FAIL") relies on COUNTIF , which counts only cells showing “FAIL” and ignores error values such as #VALUE! , so the flag shows “OK” even when a check is broken.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体通常会根据自身计算构建合理性检查，因此这些检查主要只是确认内部一致性。 例如，在任务 TheLiquidityEngine 上，Codex 中的 Astra 将每个预测值设为过去五年的平均值，然后检查 min ⁡ ( past ) ≤ forecast ≤ max ⁡ ( past ) \min(\text{past})\leq\text{forecast}\leq\max(\text{past}) 是否成立。 该检查仅使用给定的数据，而不依赖外部基准或判断，因此平均值总能通过检查。 主错误标志同样可能在某些检查已失效时仍显示「OK」，这一情况在多个智能体的数十个工作簿中反复出现。 例如，在 Grok 4.6 尝试任务 Momentum 时，标志 IF(COUNTIF(D7:D30,"FAIL")=0,"OK","FAIL") 依赖的 COUNTIF 只统计显示「FAIL」的单元格，而忽略诸如 #VALUE! 之类的错误值，因此即使某项检查已失效，该标志仍显示「OK」。

paragraphs.en: Even the top-ranked agent, Codex (GPT-6 Astra), shows these weaknesses: its sense checks compare outputs only with figures from the same workbook, it never names its key inputs, and it prefills even small models with thousands of inactive formula rows or columns (Appendix K.2.1 ).
paragraphs.zh: 即使排名最高的智能体 Codex (GPT-6 Astra) 也表现出这些弱点：其合理性检查仅将输出与同一工作簿中的数字进行比较，从不指明其关键输入，并且即使是小模型，它也会预填充数千行或列的无效公式（附录 K.2.1 ）。

paragraphs.en: We introduce MBABench-2.0, a fully public benchmark of 101 101 diverse and difficult financial spreadsheet construction tasks, developed over approximately 2,095 2{,}095 person-hours. Beyond evaluating a spreadsheet on accuracy, we propose a comprehensive taxonomy of 129 129 criteria that details what constitutes a quality spreadsheet as codified in the industry. To support grading these criteria at scale, we also develop a corresponding agentic judge and validate its reliability against human judgment. Across state-of-the-art models and all available product harnesses ( 20 20 + agents), we find even the best performing agent passes only a small fraction of tasks. We characterize how agents fail financial spreadsheet tasks in both numerical accuracy and in the high-level quality criteria we taxonomized. Overall, modern agents still fall short of delivering high-quality spreadsheets that professional settings demand. We hope MBABench-2.0 provides a transparent, scalable testbed for agent-built spreadsheets and highlights the gap between the professional standard that finance practitioners rely on and what agents currently deliver.
paragraphs.zh: 我们介绍 MBABench-2.0，这是一个完全公开的基准，包含 101 个多样且困难的金融电子表格构建任务，开发耗时约 2,095 人时。 除了评估电子表格的准确性之外，我们提出了一套包含 129 项标准的综合分类体系，详细界定了行业中所公认的高质量电子表格的构成要素。 为支持对这些标准进行大规模评分，我们还开发了相应的智能体评判器，并对照人类判断验证了其可靠性。 在最先进的模型和所有可用的产品运行环境（20 多个智能体）上，我们发现即使是表现最好的智能体也只能通过一小部分任务。 我们刻画了智能体在金融电子表格任务中于数值准确性和我们所分类的高层质量标准两方面的失败方式。 总体而言，现代智能体仍无法交付专业场景所要求的高质量电子表格。 我们希望 MBABench-2.0 能为智能体构建的电子表格提供一个透明、可扩展的测试平台，并凸显金融从业者所依赖的专业标准与智能体当前交付水平之间的差距。

sents.en: Across state-of-the-art models and all available product harnesses ( 20 20 + agents), we find even the best performing agent passes only a small fraction of tasks.
sents.zh: 在最先进的模型和所有可用的产品运行环境（20 多个智能体）上，我们发现即使是表现最好的智能体也只能通过一小部分任务。

sents.en: We characterize how agents fail financial spreadsheet tasks in both numerical accuracy and in the high-level quality criteria we taxonomized.
sents.zh: 我们刻画了智能体在金融电子表格任务中于数值准确性和我们所分类的高层质量标准两方面的失败方式。

sents.en: Overall, modern agents still fall short of delivering high-quality spreadsheets that professional settings demand.
sents.zh: 总体而言，现代智能体仍无法交付专业场景所要求的高质量电子表格。

sents.en: We hope MBABench-2.0 provides a transparent, scalable testbed for agent-built spreadsheets and highlights the gap between the professional standard that finance practitioners rely on and what agents currently deliver.
sents.zh: 我们希望 MBABench-2.0 能为智能体构建的电子表格提供一个透明、可扩展的测试平台，并凸显金融从业者所依赖的专业标准与智能体当前交付水平之间的差距。

paragraphs.en: We gratefully acknowledge the support of OpenAI, Anthropic, and the Laude Institute, whose generous backing made MBABench-2.0 possible.
paragraphs.zh: 我们衷心感谢 OpenAI、Anthropic 以及 Laude Institute 的支持，他们的慷慨资助使 MBABench-2.0 得以实现。

paragraphs.en: Task-specific rubrics would have to restate the common core of financial models for every task; they are costly to write, inconsistent across tasks, and impractical to validate per criterion. BankerToolBench [ 13 ] , for instance, uses a separate rubric for each of its 100 tasks and validates its grader only in aggregate; HealthBench [ 2 ] validates its grader per criterion only on the 34 criteria shared across conversations, not on its tens of thousands of conversation-specific ones. We instead designed a single rubric that combines universal criteria, which capture this common core, with conditional criteria, which capture what differs between models.
paragraphs.zh: 针对具体任务的评分标准将不得不为每个任务重复陈述金融模型的共同核心；编写成本高、跨任务不一致，且难以逐条标准进行验证。 例如，BankerToolBench [ 13 ] 为其 100 个任务中的每一个使用单独的评分标准，且仅在总体层面验证其评分器；HealthBench [ 2 ] 仅对跨对话共享的 34 条标准逐条验证其评分器，而对其数以万计的对话专属标准则未进行验证。 我们转而设计了一个单一的评分标准，将捕捉这一共同核心的通用标准与捕捉模型间差异的条件标准相结合。

paragraphs.en: The rubric was developed by finance experts and covers the quality dimensions they consider essential when building and reviewing spreadsheet-based financial models. It deliberately extends beyond numerical correctness: the Accuracy category accounts for only 19% of the total weight, and the remainder goes to criteria assessing, among other things, adherence to industry-standard formatting conventions, adaptability and maintainability, and formula transparency. Each criterion is scored as satisfied or violated: it is satisfied only if no mistake is found (Appendix A.2 ). In the version given to the judge, each criterion consists of a name, a description, and a characterization of good and bad practice; Appendix A.4 restates these criteria in a form intended to be read, and the verbatim rubric is available in our repository. For criteria that proved prone to misinterpretation during judge validation (Section 4.1 ), the judge additionally receives clarifying notes, for example that a cover sheet is judged by its contents rather than by its name.
paragraphs.zh: 该评分标准由金融专家制定，涵盖他们在构建和审阅基于电子表格的金融模型时认为至关重要的质量维度。 它有意超越了数值正确性的范畴：「准确性」类别仅占总权重的 19%，其余权重分配给评估行业标准格式规范的遵循程度、适应性与可维护性以及公式透明度等维度的标准。 每项标准被判定为满足或违反：只有未发现错误时才视为满足（附录 A.2）。 在提供给评判者的版本中，每项标准由名称、描述以及对良好实践和不良实践的刻画组成；附录 A.4 以便于阅读的形式重述了这些标准，逐字评分标准可在我们的代码仓库中获取。 对于在评判者验证过程中（第 4.1 节）被证明容易被误解的标准，评判者还会收到澄清说明，例如封面页应根据其内容而非其名称来评判。

paragraphs.en: Of the 129 129 criteria, 93 are universal and apply to every task; the remaining 36 are conditional and apply only to tasks whose models require the feature they check. These features include circular references (e.g., Circularity -- valid justification ), multiple business units ( Multi-unit coverage ), alternative accounting treatments ( Capitalization switches ), stub periods ( Stub period handling ), a non-calendar fiscal year ( Real fiscal year handling ), a time dimension (e.g., Single date driver or Chronological left-to-right ), multiple scenarios ( Cross-scenario summary ), and a workbook large enough to need navigation ( Linked table of contents ). Table 3 lists all conditional criteria by category; Accuracy, Formulas, Purpose & Scope, and Rounding contain only universal criteria.
paragraphs.zh: 在这 129 项标准中，有 93 项是通用标准，适用于所有任务；其余 36 项是条件性标准，仅适用于模型需要其所检查功能的任务。 这些功能包括循环引用（例如，Circularity -- valid justification）、多个业务单元（Multi-unit coverage）、备选会计处理方法（Capitalization switches）、不完整期间（Stub period handling）、非日历财年（Real fiscal year handling）、时间维度（例如，Single date driver 或 Chronological left-to-right）、多种情景（Cross-scenario summary），以及大到需要导航的工作簿（Linked table of contents）。 表 3 按类别列出了所有条件性标准；Accuracy、Formulas、Purpose & Scope 和 Rounding 仅包含通用标准。

paragraphs.en: For each task, its author annotated which of the 36 conditional criteria apply to the model the task requires; universal criteria apply by definition. The annotation was completed before grading and does not depend on any agent’s output. A criterion annotated as not applicable is neither presented to the judge nor scored for that task, and its weight is redistributed within its category (Appendix A.2 ). Between 12 and 33 conditional criteria apply to each task, so that each task is graded on between 105 and 126 criteria. Because every category contains at least one universal criterion, all 12 12 categories contribute to the score of every task.
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个任务，其作者标注了 36 项条件性准则中有哪些适用于该任务所要求的模型；通用性准则按定义自动适用。 标注工作在评分开始前完成，不依赖于任何智能体的输出。 被标注为不适用的准则既不会呈现给评审，也不会在该任务中被计分，其权重会在所属类别内部重新分配（附录 A.2）。 每个任务适用的条件性准则在 12 到 33 项之间，因此每个任务的评分依据在 105 到 126 项准则之间。 由于每个类别都至少包含一项通用性准则，全部 12 个类别都会计入每个任务的得分。

paragraphs.en: The experts also assigned each criterion to one of 12 12 categories, which group criteria by the aspect of the workbook they assess, and to one of four importance levels, which reflect how strongly a violation impairs the workbook. Appendix A.4 introduces each category, and Appendix A.2 describes how categories and importance levels are converted into weights. Of the 129 129 criteria, 12 are ultra important, 41 highly important, 52 important, and 24 not absolutely crucial (Table 2 ).
paragraphs.zh: 专家们还将每条准则归入12个类别之一，这些类别按工作簿所评估的方面对准则进行分组，并归入四个重要性级别之一，以反映违规对工作簿的损害程度。 附录A.4介绍了每个类别，附录A.2描述了类别和重要性级别如何转换为权重。 在129条准则中，12条为极重要，41条为非常重要，52条为重要，24条为并非绝对关键（表2）。

paragraphs.en: Final calculation accuracy is graded deterministically by comparing the agent’s answers on the questions tab with those of the golden solution; a single wrong, missing, or hardcoded answer violates the criterion. The equivalence rules given in its description (Appendix A.4 ) disregard differences of form: an answer counts as correct if it rounds to the correct value at the required precision, differs only in display (e.g., a percentage given as a fraction, a negative number in parentheses, or a different date format), or, for costs and other outflows, differs only in sign. A different unit scale, such as thousands instead of millions, is never accepted. Of the other criteria, 19 are checked deterministically by fixed rules and the remaining 109 by the agentic judge (Appendix F ).
paragraphs.zh: 最终计算准确性通过将智能体在问题选项卡上的答案与黄金标准方案的答案进行比较来进行确定性评分；只要有一个答案错误、缺失或是硬编码的，即违反该准则。 其描述中给出的等价规则（附录 A.4）不考虑形式上的差异：如果答案按要求精度四舍五入后数值正确、仅在显示形式上不同（例如百分比写成小数、负数放在括号中、或日期格式不同），或者对于成本及其他支出仅在符号上不同，则该答案视为正确。 不同的数量级单位（例如以千代替百万）永远不会被接受。 在其余准则中，19 项由固定规则进行确定性检查，另外 109 项由智能体评审员（附录 F）检查。

paragraphs.en: The rubric itself is not disclosed to the agents. Instead, the house standards (Appendix G ) state the conventions behind several criteria that vary between organizations, such as the change log, the linked table of contents, the checks tab with a single flag on the cover, and the sign convention, without revealing the criteria or their weights. The rubric encodes principles shared across public codes [ 9 ] ; the house standards fix the conventions those codes leave open, so that criteria such as Consistent sign convention have a single correct target.
paragraphs.zh: 评分细则本身不会透露给智能体。 取而代之的是，机构标准（附录 G）说明了若干在组织之间存在差异的准则背后的约定，例如变更日志、带链接的目录、封面上带单个标志的检查标签页，以及符号约定，但不透露这些准则或其权重。 该评分细则编码了公开代码中共享的原则 [ 9 ]；机构标准则固定了这些代码未作规定的约定，使得诸如「符号约定一致」之类的准则具有唯一正确的目标。

paragraphs.en: This design combines the coverage of task-specific rubrics with the rigor of a single shared rubric. Comprehensive. Universal criteria set a common quality bar, while conditional criteria capture model-specific requirements, so every applicable rubric criterion is checked for every task, whatever model it requires. Efficient and extensible. A new task requires no new criteria, only a yes/no relevance decision per conditional criterion, and even a new model type needs only the few criteria specific to it. Verifiable. Because each criterion is defined once for all tasks, the judge can be tested on each criterion individually (Section 4.1 ); and because each category carries the same weight in every task, the grading scale stays consistent across tasks and types of financial models.
paragraphs.zh: 该设计结合了任务专用评分标准的覆盖面与单一共享评分标准的严谨性。全面性。 通用标准设定了统一的质量门槛，而条件标准则捕捉特定模型的要求，因此每个任务都会检查每一条适用的评分标准，无论它要求哪种模型。 高效且可扩展。 新增任务无需新增标准，只需对每条条件标准做出是/否的相关性判断，即使新增一种模型类型也只需添加针对它的少数几条标准。可验证性。 由于每条标准对所有任务只定义一次，评审可以逐条单独测试每条标准（第4.1节）；由于每个类别在每个任务中权重相同，评分尺度在各类任务和各类金融模型之间保持一致。

paragraphs.en: The final score aggregates the 129 129 rubric criteria of Section 3 (93 universal and 36 conditionally applicable) into a single score, combining each criterion’s score with its weight. The weighting procedure itself is a fixed formula, but the constants that go into it were set by judgment. All inputs described below, as well as the assignment of criteria to categories, were determined by our finance experts.

paragraphs.en: This section describes the standard that the pass rule reflects and explains why we do not report a human baseline, i.e., the pass rate of human modelers on the same tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 本节描述通过规则（pass rule）所反映的标准，并解释为什么我们不报告人类基线，即人类建模者在相同任务上的通过率。

paragraphs.en: The pass rule requires correct results ( Final calculation accuracy ) and adherence to the modeling conventions that practitioners are trained to follow, but tolerates a limited number of violations at each importance level; this tolerance also absorbs occasional judge errors (Section 3 ). Several observations indicate that this standard is attainable: each criterion graded by the judge is satisfied by a golden solution, modified where necessary (Appendix F.2 ); the golden solutions show that every task can be solved correctly (Appendix C ); and the top agents already pass some of the tasks (Section 5 ).
paragraphs.zh: 通过规则要求结果正确（最终计算准确性）并遵循从业者受训掌握的建模惯例，但允许在每个重要性级别上存在有限数量的违规；这种容忍度也能吸收评审智能体偶发的判断错误（第 3 节）。 若干观察表明这一标准是可以达到的：评审智能体所评定的每项标准都能被一个黄金解答满足，必要时进行了修改（附录 F.2）；黄金解答表明每个任务都能被正确解决（附录 C）；而且顶尖智能体已经通过了其中一些任务（第 5 节）。

sents.en: Several observations indicate that this standard is attainable: each criterion graded by the judge is satisfied by a golden solution, modified where necessary (Appendix F.2 ); the golden solutions show that every task can be solved correctly (Appendix C ); and the top agents already pass some of the tasks (Section 5 ).

paragraphs.en: Like quality standards in practice, the pass rule is defined by what the work requires, not by how often a particular group of humans meets it. A human pass rate would also depend on choices for which no canonical setting exists: the experience of the modelers, the time they are given, and whether their work is reviewed before grading. Different choices could yield very different pass rates for the same tasks, so no single baseline would provide a stable reference point. Even for one setting, a reliable baseline would require several qualified modelers per task, and thus considerable resources. Instead, the benchmark relates its tasks to human capability through its annotations: the difficulty levels reflect the expertise each task demands (Appendix B.1 ), and the time estimates state how long a human modeler would need to build each model (Appendix B.2 ).
paragraphs.zh: 与实践中的质量标准一样，通过规则由工作本身的要求来定义，而不是由某类特定人群达到该要求的频率来定义。 人类通过率还会取决于一些没有标准设定的选择：建模者的经验、分配给他们的时间，以及他们的工作在评分前是否经过审核。 不同的选择可能使同一任务产生差异很大的人类通过率，因此任何单一基线都无法提供稳定的参考点。 即使只针对一种设定，可靠的基线也需要每项任务配备多名合格的建模者，因而需要相当可观的资源。 因此，该基准测试通过其标注将任务与人类能力联系起来：难度等级反映了每项任务所需的专业水平（附录 B.1），时间估计则说明了人类建模者构建每个模型大约需要多长时间（附录 B.2）。

sents.en: Even for one setting, a reliable baseline would require several qualified modelers per task, and thus considerable resources.
sents.zh: 即使只针对一种设定，可靠的基线也需要每项任务配备多名合格的建模者，因而需要相当可观的资源。

sents.en: Instead, the benchmark relates its tasks to human capability through its annotations: the difficulty levels reflect the expertise each task demands (Appendix B.1 ), and the time estimates state how long a human modeler would need to build each model (Appendix B.2 ).
sents.zh: 因此，该基准测试通过其标注将任务与人类能力联系起来：难度等级反映了每项任务所需的专业水平（附录 B.1），时间估计则说明了人类建模者构建每个模型大约需要多长时间（附录 B.2）。

paragraphs.en: For readability, the criteria below paraphrase the criteria given to the judge; the verbatim rubric is available in our repository.
paragraphs.zh: 为了便于阅读，下文中的评判标准是对评委所用标准的转述；逐字版本的评分标准可在我们的代码库中获取。

paragraphs.en: Each criterion is tagged with three attributes. Its level of importance is one of ultra important, highly important, important, or not absolutely crucial. A conditional criterion applies only to tasks for which it is relevant. A discounted criterion carries reduced weight because it can largely be met with what the input workbook already provides. Appendix A.2 explains how these attributes enter the weighting.
paragraphs.zh: 每个标准都带有三个属性标签。 其重要程度分为：极其重要、非常重要、重要或并非绝对关键。 条件性标准仅适用于与其相关的任务。 折减标准所占权重较低，因为输入工作簿本身已能大体满足该标准。 附录 A.2 解释了这些属性如何参与权重计算。

sents.en: Each criterion is tagged with three attributes.
sents.zh: 每个标准都带有三个属性标签。

sents.en: Its level of importance is one of ultra important, highly important, important, or not absolutely crucial.
sents.zh: 其重要程度分为：极其重要、非常重要、重要或并非绝对关键。

sents.en: A conditional criterion applies only to tasks for which it is relevant.
sents.zh: 条件性标准仅适用于与其相关的任务。

sents.en: A discounted criterion carries reduced weight because it can largely be met with what the input workbook already provides.
sents.zh: 折减标准所占权重较低，因为输入工作簿本身已能大体满足该标准。

sents.en: Appendix A.2 explains how these attributes enter the weighting.
sents.zh: 附录 A.2 解释了这些属性如何参与权重计算。

paragraphs.en: Accuracy covers whether the workbook returns the correct numbers for the task at hand, separating three parts that are frequently treated as one: correct carry-over of the task inputs, correct calculation on those inputs, and presence of every required output.
paragraphs.zh: 准确性考察的是工作簿是否为当前任务返回正确的数字，它将经常被混为一谈的三个部分区分开来：任务输入的正确承接、对这些输入的正确计算，以及所有必需输出的完整呈现。

paragraphs.en: Assumptions covers how the inputs that drive the model are held and presented. It asks whether the assumptions are gathered in one place and flow in a single direction into the calculations, whether each one is defined exactly once, and whether labels, units, and sources allow a reader to interpret and verify an input without tracing the formulas that use it.
paragraphs.zh: 假设部分涵盖驱动模型的输入是如何保存和呈现的。 它关注的问题是：假设是否集中在一处并以单一方向流入计算，每个假设是否只被定义一次，以及标签、单位和来源是否能让读者无需追踪使用该输入的公式就能解读和验证一个输入。

sents.en: Assumptions covers how the inputs that drive the model are held and presented.
sents.zh: 假设部分涵盖驱动模型的输入是如何保存和呈现的。

sents.en: It asks whether the assumptions are gathered in one place and flow in a single direction into the calculations, whether each one is defined exactly once, and whether labels, units, and sources allow a reader to interpret and verify an input without tracing the formulas that use it.
sents.zh: 它关注的问题是：假设是否集中在一处并以单一方向流入计算，每个假设是否只被定义一次，以及标签、单位和来源是否能让读者无需追踪使用该输入的公式就能解读和验证一个输入。

paragraphs.en: Documentation covers what the workbook tells a reader who did not build it. It spans the statements that frame the model as a whole, that is, its purpose, scope, methodology, design decisions, and revision history, and the navigational and explanatory material that makes the sheets usable, from tab names and a linked table of contents to a glossary of conventions and commentary on individual formulas.
paragraphs.zh: 文档部分涵盖工作簿向未参与构建它的读者所传达的内容。 它既包括将模型作为一个整体来界定的各类陈述，即其目的、范围、方法论、设计决策和修订历史，也包括使各工作表便于使用的导航性和解释性材料，从工作表标签命名和带链接的目录，到约定术语表以及对单个公式的注释说明。

sents.en: Documentation covers what the workbook tells a reader who did not build it.
sents.zh: 文档部分涵盖工作簿向未参与构建它的读者所传达的内容。

sents.en: It spans the statements that frame the model as a whole, that is, its purpose, scope, methodology, design decisions, and revision history, and the navigational and explanatory material that makes the sheets usable, from tab names and a linked table of contents to a glossary of conventions and commentary on individual formulas.
sents.zh: 它既包括将模型作为一个整体来界定的各类陈述，即其目的、范围、方法论、设计决策和修订历史，也包括使各工作表便于使用的导航性和解释性材料，从工作表标签命名和带链接的目录，到约定术语表以及对单个公式的注释说明。

paragraphs.en: Error Checks covers whether the model is internally consistent and whether it demonstrates that consistency to the reader. It combines arithmetic consistency, that is, subtotals matching the totals they roll into and a given value holding wherever it appears, with the absence of visible errors and warnings, disciplined use of error suppression, consistent units across the workbook, and the dedicated check rows, check sheet, and master flag that surface failures without manual tracing. A smaller set of issues relates to workbook hygiene, specifically file size, recalculation time, and the Name Manager.
paragraphs.zh: 错误检查考察模型在内部是否一致，以及是否向读者展示了这种一致性。 它结合了算术一致性，即分项小计与其汇总总额相符、同一数值在其出现的所有位置保持一致，还包括不存在可见的错误和警告、规范地使用错误抑制、整个工作簿中单位保持一致，以及通过专门的检查行、检查表和主标志来呈现问题而无需人工追踪。 还有较少的一类问题与工作簿的规范维护有关，具体包括文件大小、重新计算时间和名称管理器。

sents.en: Error Checks covers whether the model is internally consistent and whether it demonstrates that consistency to the reader.
sents.zh: 错误检查考察模型在内部是否一致，以及是否向读者展示了这种一致性。

sents.en: It combines arithmetic consistency, that is, subtotals matching the totals they roll into and a given value holding wherever it appears, with the absence of visible errors and warnings, disciplined use of error suppression, consistent units across the workbook, and the dedicated check rows, check sheet, and master flag that surface failures without manual tracing.
sents.zh: 它结合了算术一致性，即分项小计与其汇总总额相符、同一数值在其出现的所有位置保持一致，还包括不存在可见的错误和警告、规范地使用错误抑制、整个工作簿中单位保持一致，以及通过专门的检查行、检查表和主标志来呈现问题而无需人工追踪。

sents.en: A smaller set of issues relates to workbook hygiene, specifically file size, recalculation time, and the Name Manager.
sents.zh: 还有较少的一类问题与工作簿的规范维护有关，具体包括文件大小、重新计算时间和名称管理器。

paragraphs.en: Flexibility describes the extent to which the model can accommodate changes without having to be rebuilt. The key considerations here are whether the architecture is driver-based and formula-driven, whether time periods can be adjusted, extended, or re-granularized without manual effort, and whether the structure anticipates situations that would otherwise necessitate a redesign: the consolidation of multiple business units, a switch between capitalization and expense recognition, and the use of the model beyond its original intended purpose.
paragraphs.zh: 柔性描述的是模型在不必重建的情况下能够适应变化的程度。 这里的关键考量包括：架构是否基于驱动因素和公式驱动，时间周期能否在不需人工投入的情况下调整、延长或重新细化粒度，以及结构是否预见到那些原本需要重新设计的情形：多个业务单元的合并、资本化与费用确认之间的转换，以及模型在原本预期用途之外的使用。

sents.en: Flexibility describes the extent to which the model can accommodate changes without having to be rebuilt.
sents.zh: 柔性描述的是模型在不必重建的情况下能够适应变化的程度。

sents.en: The key considerations here are whether the architecture is driver-based and formula-driven, whether time periods can be adjusted, extended, or re-granularized without manual effort, and whether the structure anticipates situations that would otherwise necessitate a redesign: the consolidation of multiple business units, a switch between capitalization and expense recognition, and the use of the model beyond its original intended purpose.
sents.zh: 这里的关键考量包括：架构是否基于驱动因素和公式驱动，时间周期能否在不需人工投入的情况下调整、延长或重新细化粒度，以及结构是否预见到那些原本需要重新设计的情形：多个业务单元的合并、资本化与费用确认之间的转换，以及模型在原本预期用途之外的使用。

paragraphs.en: Formatting refers to the visual conventions that the workbook uses to indicate the function of each cell and the magnitude of each number. Many of these elements relate to industry-standard color coding, that is, blue for hardcoded values, black for calculations, green for cross-sheet links, and red for external references, as well as the need to exercise restraint so that additional colors, conditional formatting, borders, and shading do not conflict with this color coding. The remaining points concern number formats and finance conventions for negative numbers, zeros, separators, and currencies; the alignment and dimensions of rows and columns; and sheet- and workbook-level settings, such as zoom level, merged cells, print settings, and file format.
paragraphs.zh: 格式设置是指工作簿用来表明每个单元格的功能以及每个数字的数量级的视觉规范。 其中许多元素涉及行业标准配色，即蓝色表示硬编码数值、黑色表示计算、绿色表示跨工作表链接、红色表示外部引用，同时还需要保持克制，使额外的颜色、条件格式、边框和底纹不会与这种配色方案冲突。 其余要点涉及数字格式以及负数、零、分隔符和货币的财务惯例；行和列的对齐与尺寸；以及工作表级别和工作簿级别的设置，例如缩放比例、合并单元格、打印设置和文件格式。

sents.en: Formatting refers to the visual conventions that the workbook uses to indicate the function of each cell and the magnitude of each number.
sents.zh: 格式设置是指工作簿用来表明每个单元格的功能以及每个数字的数量级的视觉规范。

sents.en: Many of these elements relate to industry-standard color coding, that is, blue for hardcoded values, black for calculations, green for cross-sheet links, and red for external references, as well as the need to exercise restraint so that additional colors, conditional formatting, borders, and shading do not conflict with this color coding.
sents.zh: 其中许多元素涉及行业标准配色，即蓝色表示硬编码数值、黑色表示计算、绿色表示跨工作表链接、红色表示外部引用，同时还需要保持克制，使额外的颜色、条件格式、边框和底纹不会与这种配色方案冲突。

sents.en: The remaining points concern number formats and finance conventions for negative numbers, zeros, separators, and currencies; the alignment and dimensions of rows and columns; and sheet- and workbook-level settings, such as zoom level, merged cells, print settings, and file format.
sents.zh: 其余要点涉及数字格式以及负数、零、分隔符和货币的财务惯例；行和列的对齐与尺寸；以及工作表级别和工作簿级别的设置，例如缩放比例、合并单元格、打印设置和文件格式。

paragraphs.en: Formulas covers how the calculations themselves are written: which functions are used, how much logic a single cell is allowed to carry, whether the same logic is expressed identically wherever it recurs, and whether references are anchored so that a copied formula pulls the intended cells. The rubric places greater emphasis on readability and verifiability than on conciseness, since a formula that a reviewer cannot follow cannot be verified.
paragraphs.zh: 公式部分涵盖计算本身的书写方式：使用了哪些函数、单个单元格允许承载多少逻辑、相同逻辑在每次重复出现时是否以一致的方式表达，以及引用是否正确锚定，从而确保复制后的公式能取到预期的单元格。 该评分标准更强调可读性和可验证性，而非简洁性，因为审核者看不懂的公式是无法被验证的。

sents.en: Formulas covers how the calculations themselves are written: which functions are used, how much logic a single cell is allowed to carry, whether the same logic is expressed identically wherever it recurs, and whether references are anchored so that a copied formula pulls the intended cells.
sents.zh: 公式部分涵盖计算本身的书写方式：使用了哪些函数、单个单元格允许承载多少逻辑、相同逻辑在每次重复出现时是否以一致的方式表达，以及引用是否正确锚定，从而确保复制后的公式能取到预期的单元格。

sents.en: The rubric places greater emphasis on readability and verifiability than on conciseness, since a formula that a reviewer cannot follow cannot be verified.
sents.zh: 该评分标准更强调可读性和可验证性，而非简洁性，因为审核者看不懂的公式是无法被验证的。

paragraphs.en: Model Outputs & Executive Summary covers the results layer of the model, that is, the metrics it reports and the page on which they are presented. It asks whether the output metrics relevant to the model’s purpose are computed in a dedicated section, whether the results are checked for plausibility against outside reference points as part of the model rather than alongside it, and whether the summary recalculates with the inputs rather than simply presenting a manually created snapshot.
paragraphs.zh: 模型输出与执行摘要涵盖模型的结果层，即模型所报告的指标以及展示这些指标的页面。 它考查的问题是：与模型用途相关的输出指标是否在专门的章节中计算，结果是否作为模型的一部分（而非在模型之外）对照外部参考点进行了合理性检验，以及摘要是否随输入重新计算，而不是仅仅呈现一份手动制作的快照。

sents.en: Model Outputs & Executive Summary covers the results layer of the model, that is, the metrics it reports and the page on which they are presented.
sents.zh: 模型输出与执行摘要涵盖模型的结果层，即模型所报告的指标以及展示这些指标的页面。

sents.en: It asks whether the output metrics relevant to the model’s purpose are computed in a dedicated section, whether the results are checked for plausibility against outside reference points as part of the model rather than alongside it, and whether the summary recalculates with the inputs rather than simply presenting a manually created snapshot.
sents.zh: 它考查的问题是：与模型用途相关的输出指标是否在专门的章节中计算，结果是否作为模型的一部分（而非在模型之外）对照外部参考点进行了合理性检验，以及摘要是否随输入重新计算，而不是仅仅呈现一份手动制作的快照。

paragraphs.en: Potential Dangers covers the properties of a workbook that mislead a reviewer or break under use: content that is hidden rather than shown, dependencies on files outside the workbook, code that adds risk without adding capability, and settings under which displayed values need not reflect the current inputs. Two items go beyond the file itself to the model’s behavior, namely the consistency of its sign convention and its stability when assumptions are pushed to the edge of the plausible range.
paragraphs.zh: 潜在危险涵盖工作簿中会误导审阅者或在使用中失效的属性：被隐藏而非显示的内容、对工作簿外部文件的依赖、只增加风险而不增加功能的代码，以及所显示的数值可能不反映当前输入的设置。 其中有两项超出了文件本身，涉及模型的行为，即其符号约定的一致性，以及当假设被推向合理范围边缘时模型的稳定性。

sents.en: Potential Dangers covers the properties of a workbook that mislead a reviewer or break under use: content that is hidden rather than shown, dependencies on files outside the workbook, code that adds risk without adding capability, and settings under which displayed values need not reflect the current inputs.
sents.zh: 潜在危险涵盖工作簿中会误导审阅者或在使用中失效的属性：被隐藏而非显示的内容、对工作簿外部文件的依赖、只增加风险而不增加功能的代码，以及所显示的数值可能不反映当前输入的设置。

sents.en: Two items go beyond the file itself to the model’s behavior, namely the consistency of its sign convention and its stability when assumptions are pushed to the edge of the plausible range.
sents.zh: 其中有两项超出了文件本身，涉及模型的行为，即其符号约定的一致性，以及当假设被推向合理范围边缘时模型的稳定性。

paragraphs.en: Purpose & Scope holds a single item, which judges the model as a whole against the job it was built to do. Where the other categories examine components, this one asks whether the overall architecture is the right one, given that a model can satisfy every local convention and still be built at the wrong level of detail for its purpose.
paragraphs.zh: Purpose & Scope 仅包含一个条目，它将模型作为一个整体，对照其被构建时所要完成的工作进行评判。 其他类别考察的是各个组成部分，而这一类别追问的是：考虑到一个模型可以满足所有局部约定却仍然在其用途上构建于错误的细节层级，整体架构是否是正确的那个。

sents.en: Purpose & Scope holds a single item, which judges the model as a whole against the job it was built to do.
sents.zh: Purpose & Scope 仅包含一个条目，它将模型作为一个整体，对照其被构建时所要完成的工作进行评判。

sents.en: Where the other categories examine components, this one asks whether the overall architecture is the right one, given that a model can satisfy every local convention and still be built at the wrong level of detail for its purpose.
sents.zh: 其他类别考察的是各个组成部分，而这一类别追问的是：考虑到一个模型可以满足所有局部约定却仍然在其用途上构建于错误的细节层级，整体架构是否是正确的那个。

paragraphs.en: Rounding covers where in the calculation chain precision may be given up and how the resulting convention is communicated. It separates the internal treatment, where full precision must survive to the end of the chain, from the presentation of the final figures, where rounding to a sensible precision conveys the certainty the numbers actually carry.
paragraphs.zh: 舍入涉及在计算链的哪个环节可以放弃精度，以及由此形成的约定如何传达。 它将内部处理与最终数字的呈现区分开来：内部处理必须保持完整精度直到链条末端，而最终数字则以合理的精度进行舍入，以传达这些数字实际具备的确定性。

sents.en: Rounding covers where in the calculation chain precision may be given up and how the resulting convention is communicated.
sents.zh: 舍入涉及在计算链的哪个环节可以放弃精度，以及由此形成的约定如何传达。

sents.en: It separates the internal treatment, where full precision must survive to the end of the chain, from the presentation of the final figures, where rounding to a sensible precision conveys the certainty the numbers actually carry.
sents.zh: 它将内部处理与最终数字的呈现区分开来：内部处理必须保持完整精度直到链条末端，而最终数字则以合理的精度进行舍入，以传达这些数字实际具备的确定性。

paragraphs.en: Structure covers the architecture of the workbook and the layout within each sheet. At workbook level it asks which components are present, how functions are separated across tabs, how the tabs are ordered, and whether the architecture matches the entity’s fiscal calendar and the model’s deal or planning orientation. At sheet level it asks how the timeline is laid out and labeled, how calculations are grouped and headed, how labels align with the values they describe, and how balances and circular references are constructed.
paragraphs.zh: 结构涵盖工作簿的整体架构以及每个工作表内部的布局。 在工作簿层面，它考察存在哪些组成部分、功能如何在各标签页之间划分、标签页如何排序，以及该架构是否与主体的财年和模型的交易或规划导向相匹配。 在工作表层面，它考察时间轴如何布局和标注、计算如何分组和设置标题、标签如何与其所描述的数值对齐，以及余额和循环引用如何构建。

sents.en: Structure covers the architecture of the workbook and the layout within each sheet.
sents.zh: 结构涵盖工作簿的整体架构以及每个工作表内部的布局。

sents.en: At workbook level it asks which components are present, how functions are separated across tabs, how the tabs are ordered, and whether the architecture matches the entity’s fiscal calendar and the model’s deal or planning orientation.
sents.zh: 在工作簿层面，它考察存在哪些组成部分、功能如何在各标签页之间划分、标签页如何排序，以及该架构是否与主体的财年和模型的交易或规划导向相匹配。

sents.en: At sheet level it asks how the timeline is laid out and labeled, how calculations are grouped and headed, how labels align with the values they describe, and how balances and circular references are constructed.
sents.zh: 在工作表层面，它考察时间轴如何布局和标注、计算如何分组和设置标题、标签如何与其所描述的数值对齐，以及余额和循环引用如何构建。

paragraphs.en: Tasks of this kind are costly to create: each is authored from scratch by a finance expert, requires a long build time (Appendix B.2 ), and passes several review rounds (Appendix C ). Individual difficulty levels and task types therefore contain limited numbers of tasks. We accordingly focus difficulty-related findings on the harder levels jointly (Section 5 ) and use task types to describe the benchmark’s coverage rather than to compare agents across types.
paragraphs.zh: 这类任务的创建成本很高：每个任务均由金融专家从零编写，需要较长的构建时间（附录 B.2），并经过多轮审查（附录 C）。 因此，各个难度级别和任务类型所包含的任务数量有限。 有鉴于此，我们将与难度相关的发现集中在较难的级别上合并分析（第 5 节），并将任务类型用于描述基准的覆盖范围，而不是跨类型比较智能体。

sents.en: Tasks of this kind are costly to create: each is authored from scratch by a finance expert, requires a long build time (Appendix B.2 ), and passes several review rounds (Appendix C ).
sents.zh: 这类任务的创建成本很高：每个任务均由金融专家从零编写，需要较长的构建时间（附录 B.2），并经过多轮审查（附录 C）。

sents.en: Individual difficulty levels and task types therefore contain limited numbers of tasks.
sents.zh: 因此，各个难度级别和任务类型所包含的任务数量有限。

sents.en: We accordingly focus difficulty-related findings on the harder levels jointly (Section 5 ) and use task types to describe the benchmark’s coverage rather than to compare agents across types.
sents.zh: 有鉴于此，我们将与难度相关的发现集中在较难的级别上合并分析（第 5 节），并将任务类型用于描述基准的覆盖范围，而不是跨类型比较智能体。

paragraphs.en: Every task was scored in each of four categories: Scope, General Modeling, Finance Knowledge, and Implementation in Excel. For all four categories, a numerical score between 1 and 6 was assigned based on the classes described in the subsections below. The scores were then weighted, and the weighted sum was rounded to the nearest whole number to determine the overall difficulty. Halves were rounded up, so a weighted sum of 3.5 yielded level 4 (Medium-Hard). One task reached a rounded score of 6 (Very Hard); since a level containing a single task would not be representative, we reclassified it as Hard, so that no task is labeled Very Hard.
paragraphs.zh: 每个任务都在四个类别中分别评分：范围（Scope）、通用建模（General Modeling）、财务知识（Finance Knowledge）以及 Excel 实现（Implementation in Excel）。 在这四个类别中，均根据下文小节所描述的等级，赋予 1 到 6 之间的数值分数。 随后对各分数进行加权，将加权和四舍五入到最接近的整数，以确定总体难度。 半分向上取整，因此加权和为 3.5 时对应第 4 级（中偏难）。 有一个任务的取整分数达到了 6（极难）；由于仅包含单个任务的级别不具代表性，我们将其重新归类为难，因此没有任何任务被标注为极难。

paragraphs.en: Scope measures the breadth and structural complexity of the task (how many components, steps, or interdependent pieces the task contains). While it is correlated with the task solving duration, it is not derived from it alone, since it takes into account not only the extent but also the complexity.
paragraphs.zh: 范围衡量任务的广度和结构复杂度（即任务包含多少组件、步骤或相互依赖的部分）。 虽然范围与任务解决时长相关，但它并非仅由时长推导得出，因为它考虑的不仅是工作量的大小，还有复杂程度。

paragraphs.en: General Modeling measures the technical difficulty of the quantitative work itself (the sophistication of the calculations, logic, and model architecture required). The scale captures the depth of analytical rigor: how linked, layered, and error-prone the calculations are, and how much modeling knowledge and experience are required to solve the task.
paragraphs.zh: 通用建模衡量量化工作本身的技术难度（所需的计算、逻辑和模型架构的复杂程度）。 该维度捕捉分析严谨性的深度：计算之间的关联程度、层次结构和易错程度，以及解决该任务所需的建模知识与经验的多少。

paragraphs.en: The category Finance Knowledge determines how much (and to what depth) finance knowledge is needed to solve the task. This determination also incorporates potential assistance given in the task instructions, while not completely dismissing the need for finance knowledge if the instructions provide such assistance.
paragraphs.zh: 「金融知识」类别决定解决该任务需要多少金融知识（以及需要多深的程度）。 这一判定也会考虑任务说明中可能提供的辅助信息，但即使说明中提供了此类辅助，也不会完全排除对金融知识的需求。

paragraphs.en: Regardless of the overall model architecture, converting the input data into a viable solution in conjunction with financial expertise requires a certain level of proficiency in Microsoft Excel. While some tasks require only basic arithmetic in Excel, others cannot be completed without a solid understanding of the latest features.
paragraphs.zh: 无论模型整体架构如何，将输入数据结合金融专业知识转化为可行的解决方案，都需要对 Microsoft Excel 具备一定的熟练程度。 有些任务只需在 Excel 中进行基础运算即可，而另一些任务则必须深入理解最新功能才能完成。
